messages:
alex (Support): Heads up — customer ACME reported a spike of 5xxs when calling hosted inference in eu-west around 09:12 UTC. They see repeated TLS handshake timeouts and gateway 502/504s. Customer says error rate ~18% for last 20m, started right after a cert rotation window. Sharing logs they pasted from their client: 

alex (Support): customer-provided curl repro (they're hitting the public API):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" "https://api.redwood-inference.eu-west.example/v1/generate" \n  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"hello"}' --max-time 10
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.eu-west.example (1.2.3.4) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS handshake timeout
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10001 milliseconds with 0 bytes received
```

alex (Support): Also attached Gateway logs from our side (sanitized):
```
[09:11:58] gateway: upstream request failed: tls handshake timeout, conn_id=98765, peer=1.2.3.4
[09:12:03] gateway: returning 502 to client, route=/v1/generate, model=gpt-large
[09:12:10] auth: oauth validation OK for token sk_live_xxx but upstream connection failed
```

bharat (infra-oncall): I can see a brief spike in DNS resolution latency for eu-west stub resolver pool at ~09:10-09:13. CPU on the resolver nodes was OK, but we saw increased retransmits to upstream resolvers and some SERVFAILs. dns-monitor-bot also flagged intermittent query timeouts.

maria (eng-sre): pinging @bharat — do we have a cert rotation event around that time? deploy-bot, did the cert manager push anything?

deploy-bot: automated-event: cert-rotation job started for cert_id=crt-2026-09-eu-west at 2026-09-12T09:09:47Z. Rotation completed at 2026-09-12T09:11:52Z. No rollback triggered.

maria (eng-sre): OK, so cert rotated right in that window. Hypothesis: some edge nodes observed DNS timeouts to CA/OCSP endpoints or to backend resolvers during rotation, which caused outbound TLS handshakes from gateway to backend to stall and produce upstream tls handshake timeouts. Could also be a SNI mismatch on some nodes if new cert hasn't propagated to all frontends.

alex (Support): Customer reports they saw more failures when they had pinned their DNS to regional endpoint; when they retried they sometimes succeeded. They also noted client-side error message: "tls: handshake failure - server sent unexpected certificate" on one attempt.

bharat (infra-oncall): I'm pulling resolver logs. Here's a snippet from one stub: 
```
09:10:59.123 QUERY api.redwood-inference.eu-west.example A -> upstream 8.8.8.8
09:11:00.317 RETRANSMIT api.redwood-inference A (timeout)
09:11:01.410 SERVFAIL for api.redwood-inference.eu-west.example
09:11:05.879 QUERY ocsp.int-ca.example -> upstream 1.1.1.1
09:11:06.002 TCP connection to 1.1.1.1 failed: timeout
```

maria (eng-sre): That TCP timeout to OCSP/responder could explain a handshake stall if the gateway waits for stapled OCSP or tries to validate chain. We need to confirm whether our TLS stack is waiting synchronously for OCSP in the request path. @bharat can you confirm whether the gateway is configured to perform blocking OCSP lookups on cert rotate?

bharat (infra-oncall): Gateway config is set to attempt OCSP stapling refresh on cert activation; it will do best-effort but should not block new inbound sessions. However, there is an interaction: when cert changed, some nodes attempted to fetch OCSP for the new cert and those fetches went to remote responder; due to resolver timeouts those fetch attempts hit long tails and our goroutines got stuck for ~2s before DNS fallback kicked in. Combined with our low socket write timeout, some handshakes timed out overall.

maria (eng-sre): Action plan (short):
- Increase resolver retries and add a local fallback (loopback stub) for OCSP queries in eu-west immediately (bharat).
- Roll forward to ensure all frontends have the new cert and verify SNI mapping (deploy team).
- Short-term mitigation: add a transient increase to gateway handshake timeout to 5s to reduce 502s while we fix resolver flakiness (maria).

kim (Customer Billing): Customer ACME is asking about potential billing credits — they saw failed requests but wondered whether they were charged. Support: can we determine whether failed token usages resulted in billing events?

alex (Support): I checked logs — most failed requests never reached the token-metering step because gateway returned 502 before request body was ingested. We'll flag the customer for goodwill credit if they request it. tagging ops for confirmation.

bharat (infra-oncall): Implemented immediate firewall rule tweak and bumped resolver process count on eu-west stub cluster at 09:25. Added a local DNS cache on gateway nodes to short-circuit OCSP/CA lookups.

maria (eng-sre): I pushed a temporary config to bump handshake timeout to 5s and increased resolver retries from 2 -> 4 at 09:30. Monitoring now. Early signal: 5xx rate dropped from 18% -> 1.7% within 6 minutes.

alex (Support): Reached out to ACME and asked for confirmation if they still see failures and offered temporary credit. They responded: "we see significant improvement around 09:36, thanks. We'll confirm end-to-end tomorrow during our morning tests." :thumbsup:

maria (eng-sre): Follow-ups (owners):
- bharat: dig deeper into root cause of upstream resolver latency and work with network provider to harden (owner: bharat).
- infra: add local OCSP responder cache or prewarm mechanism to avoid external lookups on rotation (owner: infra team).
- deploy: verify cert rollout tooling to ensure zero-downtime activation and SNI consistency (owner: deploy team).
- support/alex: coordinate crediting conversation and schedule a postmortem with customer if they request it.

bharat (infra-oncall): filing ticket: INF-9723 "eu-west stub resolver transient timeouts during cert rotation leading to gateway handshake timeouts" with initial triage notes and logs.

alex (Support): I'll close this thread for now but keep monitoring. If anyone sees regressions, ping @maria or @bharat. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
